newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI upbeat on 1996/97 earnings outlook.
newsitem.headline: JCI upbeat on 1996/97 earnings outlook.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd said on Tuesday the outlook for earnings performance in the 1996/1997 financial was encouraging amid steady global commodity prices and a favourable exchange rate.
"International commodity prices for gold, coal and antimony are steady, although ferrochrome prices have weakened," JCI said.
"If the current exchange rate is maintained this alone should generate good earnings growth for JCI," it said in a statement accompanying its results for the year ended June 30.
A further weakening in the exchange rate would, however, add to inflationary cost pressures in the medium term, it said.
JCI on Tuesday reported headline earnings of 234 cents a share in the year to June 30 rising from 178 cents a year ago. Equity accounted earnings climbed to 457 cents a share from 192 cents.
A final dividend of 53 cents was declared lifting the total dividend for the year to 77 cents, up from 40 cents a year ago. Directors have also declared a capitalisation share award.

Business process re-engineering exercises and development programmes at its mines would soon have a positive effect on earnings growth, JCI said. "Such benefits are over and above potential improvements from implementation of full calender operations."
